Job Description

Are You Ready to Make It Happen at Mondelēz International?

Join our Mission to Lead the Future of Snacking. Make It Matter.

As an organization we are committed to developing the next generation of Makers and Bakers. Joining us at an early career stage in our fast paced and ever changing environment will enable you to do more, learn more and grow more. You will be encouraged to step outside your comfort zone– you may even surprise yourself! We will ensure you are given the support you need to be at your best and enable you to be yourself and bring passion and personality. Here you can lean in and speak up and bring your own flavor.

Mondelēz International was recognized as one of the Top 100 Intern Programs in the US in 2026 by Yello & WayUp and one of the Best Companies for New Graduates by Forbes.

Function Job Description

As part of Manufacturing, you’ll use your skills, our systems, and a wide array of raw materials to help create the delicious, finished products our consumers love. While taking ownership in your area of work, you’ll also ensure the safety of yourself and your colleagues while producing our top-quality products reliably and efficiently within our integrated supply chain.

As a Manufacturing - Process Engineer Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, working closely with site engineering, operations, and production teams to improve the efficiency, reliability, and overall performance of manufacturing processes. A significant portion of the internship will be spent on the production floor, building an understanding of how products are manufactured, observing day-to-day operations, attending production and control meetings, and identifying opportunities to improve how our lines and equipment operate.

Throughout the internship, you may support projects focused on process optimization, loss analysis, waste reduction, equipment performance, and production efficiency. This could include analyzing production data and line performance, identifying sources of downtime or material loss, investigating root causes, and partnering with site teams to develop and implement solutions. Interns may also have the opportunity to lead or participate in Kaizen events and other continuous improvement initiatives, using methodologies and principles such as Lean Six Sigma, World Class Manufacturing (WCM), and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM).

Projects may also include updating process maps for specific areas of the plant, evaluating production or packaging processes, optimizing key pieces of equipment, and supporting improvements to standard operating procedures. Interns may work directly with operators and technical teams to understand current processes and help update process documentation, training materials, work instructions, or operating manuals to ensure improvements can be effectively implemented and sustained.

This internship is designed to provide exposure to the full manufacturing environment; from understanding what happens directly on the production line to using data and continuous improvement tools to solve real operational challenges. Interns will collaborate cross-functionally with production, engineering, maintenance, quality, and other site teams while developing practical experience in process engineering, problem solving, manufacturing excellence, and continuous improvement.

Requirements and Preferred Qualifications

- Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in: Mechanical Engineering (preferred), Industrial Engineering (preferred), Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations and related fields.

- Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree with a preferred expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2029.

- Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with Mondelēz International (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status.

The ideal candidate displays some of the following characteristics:

- Strong leadership potential and student leadership experience.

- Excellent communication skills and resilience.

- Adaptable, with interpersonal savvy and engaged in diverse extracurricular activities.

- Demonstrating a growth mindset, agility, integrity, and a vision for the future.

- Strong cognitive abilities, willingness to learn, and data pattern recognition.

- Driven, curious, and ready to make a positive impact.

Why choose Mondelez International?

Ever wondered how your favorite snacks get made? Don’t miss the chance to find out! Check out some of the perks of being a MDLZ Intern:

- Subsidized, fully furnished housing for the Summer (For those who qualify)

- Roundtrip travel covered at the beginning and end of the internship

- Given value added projects that are presented to Leadership

- Intern programming, including events and activities throughout the summer

- Full-Time conversion opportunities upon graduation

Compensation

- The expected compensation weekly pay ranges for interns is $1,000 - $1,260, based on your expected graduation date.

- Compensation rates for Summer Interns is pre-determined and non-negotiable.

Business Unit Summary

The United States is the largest market in the Mondelēz International family with a significant employee and manufacturing footprint. Here, we produce our well-loved household favorites to provide our consumers with the right snack, at the right moment, made the right way. We have corporate offices, sales, manufacturing, and distribution locations throughout the U.S. to ensure our iconic brands—including Oreo and Chips Ahoy! cookies, Ritz, Wheat Thins and Triscuit crackers, Clif bars and Swedish Fish and Sour Patch Kids confectionery products —are close at hand for our consumers across the country.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for participation in a highly competitive bonus program with possibility for overachievement based on performance and company results.

The ideal candidate will have strong machine learning, data science and software engineering skills, some experience with modern NLP, and a curiosity about finance and trading.

Responsibilities may include:

- Using NLP to construct features from varied datasets

- Formulating research hypotheses to derive alpha

- Building and testing the performance of trading signals based on NLP and financial features

- Launching identified signals into production

- Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD candidate in computer science or other quantitative discipline

- Proficient in Python and general software engineering principles (github, testing, dev workflow)

- Strong understanding of machine learning and statistics

- Prior research experience preferred

- Experience with deep learning, specifically NLP (PyTorch, HuggingFace, LLMs, etc.) preferred

- Data science stack familiarity preferred

- An interest in financial markets

- Great attitude

- A collaborative mindset

- Commitment to the highest ethical standards

Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. We aim to attract and retain the industry’s brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people’s long-term growth.

Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX.

What You Will Do

Collins Aerospace is seeking motivated Software Engineers join the Integrated Applications Engineering team supporting development of the Collins Flight Deck. This role offers the opportunity to work on real avionics programs and gain hands-on experience across the software lifecycle—from requirements and architecture through integration, verification, and delivery.

This position will provide you the opportunity to work with Flight Deck software in an agile team environment. The team has an array of technical tasks available meant to develop engineers for the future. As part of the team, you will work alongside experienced engineers to help develop the software based on high-level system behaviors, decompose requirements, support avionics architecture development, and contribute to software verification activities. This is a strong fit for those who enjoy solving technical problems, learning complex systems, and collaborating across software, systems, and test disciplines.

Immerse yourself in a full-time, Monday-Friday co-op session, that will run January-August (including the Spring semester; it is expected students will take a semester off from coursework to fully engage with this working mentorship opportunity)

- Collaborate with a cross-functional team of software engineers, integration specialists, and test engineers to design, develop, and deliver robust avionics software solutions.
- Support the development, analysis, and refinement of software requirements and interfaces to ensure alignment with system-level objectives.
- Contribute to the planning and development of software verification and testing strategies to ensure implementations meet functional and performance requirements.
- Participate in technical reviews of software requirements, design documents, and test procedures, incorporating feedback to improve the quality and effectiveness of your deliverables.
- Assist with software integration, debugging, and issue resolution in development, simulation, and testing environments.
- Clearly communicate technical progress, challenges, and potential solutions to team members, mentors, and stakeholders to ensure alignment and successful project outcomes

What You Will Learn

- How avionics systems are developed across the full engineering lifecycle, from concept and requirements through integration and verification.
- How to work with software requirements, architecture artifacts, and verification methods used on real aerospace programs.
- How to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary engineering environment with mentorship from a dedicated technical “copilot” and other experienced team members.
- How to apply structured problem solving, technical communication, and engineering rigor in a safety-critical domain.

Qualifications We Prefer

- Must be pursuing Bachelor’s or Advanced degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM discipline. and actively enrolled through the completion of the internship/co-op session.
- Must have a minimum of 60 hours of credit by the start of the internship / co-op session.
- Experience in C/C++ and Python
- Experience may be obtained through on-the-job experience, research, coursework, or projects.

Qualifications We Prefer

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
- Prior RTX internship, co-op, or work experience.

What We Offer

- Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.
- Relocation Eligibility

Location: Plant 10-Fond du Lac, WI

Workplace Category: onsite

Innovation is the heart of Brunswick. See how your contributions will help transform vision into reality:

Position Overview:

Co-op provides an opportunity to join the fast-paced Connected Operations and Analytics (CO&A) team. This position will be integral in supporting systems, application, and analytics development for Mercury Marine Global Operations. Candidate needs to be self-starter with passion for data-driven culture, analytics, and systems/application development.

Working in a partnership with subject matter experts the CO&A team is responsible for connecting, collecting, analyzing, and publishing data from operational equipment and systems within multiple manufacturing plants. This work will help digitize Mercury’s manufacturing process. This Co-op position will support Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Industry 4.0 (I4.0) initiatives. Initial responsibilities will be focused on backlog of feature development for ongoing projects in CO&A iterative/agile workflow. Role provides opportunities for expanded responsibilities in Systems Engineering, Project Management, APIs, Microsoft Power Apps, Power BI, Database Administration, Data Science/Engineering, and Advanced Analytics (ML/AI) development.

At Brunswick, we have passion for our work and a distinct ability to deliver.

Essential Functions:

- Work with full-time team members located in multiple different operational plants, assisting with projects and analysis

- Collaborate with Systems and Analytics Engineers, Controls/Automation Engineers, Architects, Data Scientists, and Data Engineers across the business per project

- Connect, collect, and analyze data come from different types of operational equipment

- Utilize SQL queries to help retrieve data stored in databases (on-site and cloud/Azure)

- Create operational dashboards, data visualizations, and reporting

- Create Realtime Dashboards via Ignition by Inductive Automation

- Historical (trending) via Power BI by Microsoft

- Develop software applications to help collect or deliver data to many manufacturing personnel throughout the organization

- Participate in regular updates with management within the different plants

- Data processing and analysis with scripting languages (R, Python)

In addition to a great hands-on learning experience, you will also acquire the skills needed to:

- Work within an agile/scrum/iterative workflow to meet timelines

- Prioritize feature development driven from business value

- Effectively and quickly collect and analyze data coming from IIoT devices and manufacturing equipment

- Understand data storage and retrieval processes in large-scale manufacturing databases and business systems

- Analyze data and make recommendations that effectively improve process costs

- Effectively express your ideas, influence people, manage potentially contentious situations to a positive result and communicate with employees at all levels of an organization

Diversity of thought and experiences is fundamental when imagining the unimaginable. Certain skillsets/experiences are necessary; however, others can be developed along the way.

- Current enrollment in a BS program with a major in Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a relevant degree with a controls/systems/analytics emphasis

- Ability to quickly learn Ignition (Inductive Automation) and Power BI (Microsoft) software

- Training provided as needed

- Minimum second semester sophomore status with 48 completed credits

- Availability to work full-time (40 or more hours per week) through a full co-op term running January to August 2027 or May to December 2027

- The ability to enroll in a formalized co-op Program through your university

- Dependable, self-motivated, and engaged learner

- Ability to occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.

- Prior experience with SQL, relational databases, or data analysis projects

- Familiarity with Python, R, Java, or C

- Exposure to industrial automation, manufacturing systems, PLCs, SCADA, or IIOT Technologies

- Coursework or project experience involving data analytics, machine learning, statistics, or artificial intelligence

- Experience working with REST APIs, web services, or system integrations

- Experience with source control systems such as Git or Azure DevOps

- Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills demonstrated through academic, personal, or professional projects.

- Feedback and Performance Reviews: As a co-op or intern, you will receive feedback and performance reviews throughout your assignment. We value the importance for interns to understand their progress and areas for improvement.

About The Role:

As a Modeling & Simulation Software Engineering Intern you will work with the software team to develop performant modeling and simulation code for our 6DOF SITL simulation using Julia. You'll Interface with the Flight Software, HMI, and Flight Sciences teams to meet stakeholder needs and ensure accurate results. Your work will involve creating hardware/physics informed software models and validate results with real data.

Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April)

Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August)

Responsibilities:

- Develop performant simulation code for 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DOF) Software-in-the-Loop (SITL) systems using Julia.

- Develop user driven features and focus on scalability of our Monte Carlo simulation

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Flight Software, Human-Machine Interface (HMI), and Flight Sciences to align simulation outputs with stakeholder requirements.

- Design and implement physics-informed models that accurately represent hardware behavior and system dynamics.

- Validate simulation accuracy by comparing model outputs with real-world flight data and refining models accordingly.

- Optimize simulation performance to ensure real-time execution and scalability across different test environments.

- Participate in code reviews and testing cycles to maintain high software quality and reliability.

- Document modeling assumptions, validation results, and integration workflows for internal knowledge sharing and future development.

Requirements:

- Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field.

- Proficiency in Julia or strong experience with scientific computing languages such as Python, MATLAB, or C++.

- Understanding of 6DOF dynamics and simulation principles, especially in aerospace or robotics contexts.

- Familiarity with modeling physical systems, including hardware-in-the-loop or physics-informed simulation techniques.

- Experience with data validation and analysis, including comparing simulation outputs to real-world data.

- Strong understanding of engineering first principles

- Demonstrated ability to work within cross-functional teams

- Enthusiasm for aviation and Hermeus' mission

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- GPA of 3.0 or above

As a Yield Technology Equipment Engineer Intern at Micron, you will learn about the optical, x-ray, profile, and eBeam equipment used in innovative solutions to detect sources of variation in next generation memory solutions. The goal of this internship is to become familiar with in line and lab inspection equipment to help develop new solutions for efficiency and tool performance. We need engineers who are passionate about detecting problems and making changes for the better and seek out innovative ways in how to do things. We will assign you a project to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Your research tasks are designed to optimize and improve predictability of Metrology and RDA's operations. Through this project we will provide the opportunity for you to collaborate with engineers across process control, data science, yield analysis, and metrology. At the end of the period, we want the cohort to have a deep understanding of the processes, detection capabilities, and measurement strategies used in today’s semiconductor defect analysis department. We will enable this with groundbreaking strategies and next generation equipment. This is opportunity to start in the spring and goes through the summer. This position will be located in Boise, ID.

Responsibilities:

- Reviewing and analyzing experimental process flows looking for defect anomalies and quarantining process tools that are out of control
- Possess a continuous improvement process (CIP) demeanor, looking for ways to improve operations, and how to make a difference today! We want our intern to recognize, identify, and raise awareness of process anomalies with the motivation of "who needs to know this now!"
- We want our intern to use inline process signals to drive process improvements.
- Strong understanding of Aritificial Intelligence (AI) agents, Claude Code, Large Language Models, and how to utilize and optimize their efficiency.
- Work with new detection tools and inspection strategies to localize and identify process issues with the mentality of "how can this improve the model?"
- Build and improve upon techniques and identify new ways to use existing tools in order to identify relevant process issues.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, or related field. Must be a current student, must not graduate before September 2027.
- We need an intern drawn to creative problem solving and innovative solutions.
- We need someone who will investigate process anomalies, root cause analysis, data manipulation, and correlations.
- The shown ability to innovate and drive effective change in an energizing environment

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience running Scanning Electron Microscope and/or Focused Ion Beam tools.
- Proactive and passionate about learning (training and coursework).
- Excellent technical, communication, and analytical skills.
